ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $AB=AC$, $AD=AE$, $\angle BAC=\angle DAE$, $\angle 1=30^\circ$, $\angle 2=40^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle 3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BAC=\angle DAE$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC-\angle DAC=\angle DAE-\angle DAC$, i.e., $\angle BAD=\angle CAE$,\\
thus $\triangle ABD\cong \triangle ACE\ (SAS)$,\\
hence $\angle ABD=\angle 2=40^\circ$,\\
since $\angle 1=30^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle 3=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is above, B is on the left, C is below, and E is on the right; segment AC extends from A through D to C, and segment BE extends from B through D to E, so D is the intersection point of AC and BE. Angle 1 is marked at point A as ∠BAD, angle 2 is marked at point C as ∠ACE, and angle 3 is marked at point D, located between the extension line DE of BD and DA, and is the exterior angle of triangle ABD at point D. Reasoning: It is known that AB=AC, AD=AE, and ∠BAC=∠DAE. Because after removing ∠DAC, which is contained/corresponds in both ∠BAC and ∠DAE, we can get ∠BAD=∠CAE. Thus triangle ABD and triangle ACE satisfy AB=AC, AD=AE, and included angle ∠BAD=∠CAE, so by SAS we can get △ABD≅△ACE. Corresponding angles are equal, therefore ∠ABD=∠ACE=angle 2=40°. Also angle 1=∠BAD=30°. In triangle ABD, angle 3 is the exterior angle at point D, so angle 3=∠BAD+∠ABD=30°+40°=70°.
